newsitem.title: USA: Florida stripper wants day job back.
newsitem.headline: Florida stripper wants day job back.

text.p: Data processor by day, exotic dancer by night, Sandra Meyer lost both her jobs because of one swift police raid.

Meyer, 41, has been under suspension without pay for five months from her day job at the Broward County State Attorney's Office pending an investigation of her moonlighting, the Sun Sentinel of Fort Lauderdale reported on Wednesday.
"I did lead a secret life," Meyer told the newspaper. "By day I was just a little peon clerical worker. After that I was a party girl. But I didn't hurt anyone."

Meyer, who was known as Velvet at the studio where she took off her negligee for men in private booths, was at work at the prosecutor's office when sheriff's deputies raided and padlocked the club on Jan. 29.

But investigators found her dancer's license at the studio and she was questioned by investigators, who were surprised to learn she worked in law enforcement. She was suspended within a week and remains off the job.

The State Attorney's Office declined comment on specifics of Meyer's case but spokeswoman Monica Hofheinz told the Sun Sentinel employees must report off-duty jobs. "We certainly would not have approved such employment," she said.

Police said a three-month undercover investigation had turned up evidence that women at the studio provided sex for money. Meyer was not arrested but the owner of the club was charged with living from the earnings of prostitution.
Meyer said she made less than $20,000 a year at the state attorney's office and more than $60,000 at the club. The nine-year employee of the state attorney's office said she wants her day job back.
"They won't even give me unemployment," she said. "I need a steady salary as soon as possible."
